newsitem.title: USA: Ten percent of Nazi gold may be from victims.
newsitem.headline: Ten percent of Nazi gold may be from victims.

text.p: Research is showing that about 10 percent of the gold looted by the Nazis during the Second World War could have came from concentration camp victims, according to an internal World Jewish Congress memorandum.

The memo, parts of which were obtained by Reuters on Wednesday, came a week after an 11-agency U.S. government report formally confirmed that the Nazis sold Switzerland and other neutral nations gold looted from individuals along with gold stolen from the national treasuries of the European nations they occupied.

The U.S. government report said Switzerland bought $400 million in looted gold from the Nazis, but did not make an estimate of how much of that came from individual victims. Switzerland denied it knew it was buying such gold.
Jewish community sources said the WJC's 10 percent estimate could be important in determining the scope of Switzerland's effort to make restitution to Holocaust victims.
The Swiss have placed nearly $200 million in a special fund for Holocaust victims. The 10 percent projection would mean an approporiate restitution figure of about $400 million, the sources said.
"In a certain sense this is helpful to Switzerland because it puts a determined cap in so far as restitution for the looted gold is concerned," one Jewish source said.

Meanwhile, a WJC source confirmed the existence of the memo but said the figure of 10 percent was a projection based on available evidence and subject to further anaylsis and refinement. "We are not making any demands based on these figures," the WJC source stressed.

The WJC memo makes its 10 percent estimate partly on smelting records but more importantly, on the inventory of the gold hidden by the Nazis in a salt mine in Merkers in western Germany that was found by the Allies just after the war ended.
The Merkers find staggered the Allies.

Soliders found some $300 million worth of gold -- worth $3 billion today -- in a cave filled with paintings and other loot. Merkers represented 93 percent of the gold recovered by the Allies from the Nazis after the war.

The internal memo cites Allied documents as saying the Germans divided up their gold into monetary gold, including gold coins and gold bars, and SS gold that was confiscated from concentration camp victims. In a document dated July 10, 1945, the U.S. Army placed the value of non-monetary gold found there at 10 percent of the total.

The monetary gold assets at Merkers was placed at $239 million at 1945 prices and included $125 million in the form of gold coins and $114 million in bar form. In addition there were 207 containers of SS loot, including jewelry, gold items and gold extracted from the teeth of death camp inmates.
The WJC said it was able to trace the smelting records of 76 gold bars found at Merkers and discovered that seven of those bars were cast from SS loot taken from concentration camp victims.
A total of 8,346 gold bars were found at Merkers, but the smelting records of all of these have either not been found or not been examined.

A secret 1946 letter from the U.S. embassy in Paris to the secretary of state asked that the gold bars at Merkers be assayed to determine "if they represent melted down gold teeth fillings." The assay was never carried out.
